c.tagline: Gateway to the Japan Alps — the black 'Crow Castle' and wasabi-fed mountain streams.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable but pricey; there is no Uber ride-share, and apps such as GO and DiDi simply dispatch regular metered taxis. For sightseeing most visitors use the Town Sneaker loop bus, Alpico buses and the Matsumoto Dentetsu line instead.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance; 119 operators can often arrange English-language support.

hood_desc: The castle district north of the Metoba river, home to the black National-Treasure Matsumoto Castle, the city museum and municipal offices; central and packed with the must-see sights.
A preserved merchant street of white-walled kura storehouses now full of craft shops, sake breweries and cafes; atmospheric and full of boutique browsing.
The riverside 'Frog Street' lined with tiny stalls, antique shops and the Yohashira Shrine; quirky, characterful and best explored by day.
The modern transport hub around Matsumoto Station, with the main hotels, department stores and bus terminals; the convenient walkable base for arrivals and onward trips.
A historic hot-spring quarter in the north-eastern foothills, once the bath of the Matsumoto castle lords, with ryokan and public baths; quiet and restful.

water.note: Tap water is excellent Alpine-sourced and safe everywhere.

transit.hours: The Town Sneaker and city buses run roughly 8:00am-6/7pm; trains run from early morning to around midnight, after which taxis are the only option.
transit.note: The castle, Nakamachi and Nawate are all an easy walk from the station, so most visitors only need buses for Asama Onsen or trains onward to the Alps, Kamikochi and Nagano.
transit.pay: City buses are pay-on-board in cash (IC cards such as Suica are only slowly rolling out on Alpico buses, so carry coins); the Town Sneaker loop is ¥200 a ride or ¥500 for a day pass. JR and Matsumoto Dentetsu trains take IC cards and tickets from station machines.

bus: Matsumoto Bus Terminal (Alpico highway coaches to Tokyo/Nagoya/Osaka)
train: Matsumoto Station (JR Azusa Ltd Express to Tokyo/Shinjuku)

transit.m: Alpico airport shuttle bus to Matsumoto Station (~25 min, meets flights)
Taxi to the city centre (~20-25 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is simply included in the price.

food.name: Shinshu soba
food.desc: Nagano's buckwheat noodles, often nearly pure soba, served cold on a bamboo zaru with dipping broth, wasabi and spring onion, finished with the cooking water.

places.name: Marushu
places.note: Small soba house praised for handmade noodles and warm hospitality.

places.name: Izakaya Gabuto
places.note: Central izakaya known for Shinshu soba alongside local drinking food.

places.name: Soba shops of Nakamachi street
places.note: Old white-walled merchant street lined with soba counters near the castle.

food.name: Basashi
food.desc: Raw horse sashimi, a Nagano speciality, sliced thin and eaten with grated ginger, garlic and sweet soy; fattier cuts are marbled like tuna.

places.name: Alps Horno
places.note: Central restaurant known for its basashi plates and Shinshu drinking food.

places.name: Yamameya
places.note: Skewer house that also serves horse sashimi and sanzoku-yaki.

places.name: Izakayas of Nawate-dori
places.note: Frog street beside the river; several small izakaya list basashi.

food.name: Sanzoku-yaki
food.desc: Bandit's grill: a whole chicken thigh marinated in garlic soy, dusted in potato starch and deep-fried until huge and crackling, served with cabbage.

places.name: Ippo Ippo
places.note: Specialises in sanzoku-yaki on the riverside frog street by the castle.

places.name: Yamameya
places.note: Serves the Nagano classic alongside yakitori and soba.

places.name: Sanzoku
places.note: Mountain restaurant south of the city credited with the original dish; big portions.

food.name: Oyaki
food.desc: Buckwheat or wheat dumplings stuffed with nozawana pickled greens, aubergine, pumpkin or sweet bean, then steamed and griddled. Nagano farm food.

places.name: Rairaitei Matsumoto
places.note: Oyaki specialist a short walk from the castle; several fillings daily.

places.name: Miyota
places.note: Central shop selling freshly griddled oyaki to take away.

places.name: Nawate-dori stalls
places.note: Street stalls sell oyaki and taiyaki to eat while walking the old lane.

food.name: Shinshu miso dishes
food.desc: Matsumoto is miso country: rice miso goes into soup, miso ramen, dengaku glazed tofu and grilled miso-basted rice balls.

places.name: Ishii Miso
places.note: Historic brewery still ageing miso in wooden barrels; tours and tasting shop.

places.name: Shizuka
places.note: Old wood-beamed izakaya doing oden, miso dishes and set meals.

places.name: Soba shops of Nakamachi street
places.note: Many pair soba with miso soup and miso-grilled rice balls.

food.name: Sansai, wasabi and nozawana
food.desc: Mountain vegetables tempura-fried or dressed, fresh wasabi grated at the table, and nozawana pickled greens served with almost every meal.

places.name: Daio Wasabi Farm
places.note: Huge spring-fed wasabi farm 30 minutes away, with wasabi soba and ice cream.

places.name: Shizuka
places.note: Traditional izakaya with sansai side dishes and pickles on the menu.

places.name: Marushu
places.note: Soba served with mountain-vegetable tempura in season.

food.name: Shinshu jizake
food.desc: Nagano is Japan's second sake prefecture; alpine snowmelt makes clean dry sake, brewed in Matsumoto and neighbouring valleys and served hot or chilled.

places.name: Oyama Brewery
places.note: City-centre sake brewery with a shop counter for tasting local brews.

places.name: Shizuka
places.note: Long-standing izakaya with a good list of Nagano sake by the glass.

places.name: Sake shops of Nakamachi street
places.note: Merchant-street sellers stock jizake from breweries across Shinshu.

food.name: Shinshu wine and apple juice
food.desc: Kikyogahara and Azumino vineyards make Merlot and Concord wines, while Nagano's orchards press some of Japan's best apple juice and cider.

places.name: Wineries of Kikyogahara
places.note: Nagano's oldest wine district, a short train ride south; tastings at the estates.

places.name: Izakaya Gabuto
places.note: Local wine and sake poured alongside soba and grilled dishes.

places.name: Nawate-dori stalls
places.note: Shops selling apple juice, cider and fruit products from Nagano orchards.

landmarks: Matsumoto Castle
Japan's oldest surviving five-tier keep, the black-walled 'Crow Castle' floats on its moat against snow-capped Northern Alps, a National Treasure.
Nakamachi Street
A preserved merchant street of black-and-white namako-walled storehouses, now housing sake shops, craft galleries and inviting cafés.
Nawate-dori (Frog Street)
A quirky riverside lane of old-fashioned stalls and frog statuary leading toward the castle, beloved for snacks and retro souvenirs.
Matsumoto City Museum of Art
Hometown shrine to Yayoi Kusama, its polka-dotted facade and permanent collection celebrate the avant-garde queen alongside regional artists.
Former Kaichi School
An 1876 pseudo-Western schoolhouse of pastel plaster and cherub-carved gables, a National Treasure of Meiji-era educational architecture.
Yohashira Shrine
The city-center Shinto shrine honoring four deities, its serene grounds hosting Matsumoto's liveliest festivals beside the Metoba River.
Japan Ukiyo-e Museum
One of the world's great woodblock-print collections, over 100,000 works amassed by the merchant Sakai family across ten generations.
Daio Wasabi Farm (Azumino)
Japan's largest wasabi farm spreads emerald cultivation beds along crystal spring streams, with waterwheels featured in Kurosawa's 'Dreams'.
Kamikochi
The sublime alpine valley gateway in Chubu-Sangaku National Park, where the Azusa River mirrors Hotaka's peaks from iconic Kappa Bridge.
Utsukushigahara Highlands
A 2,000-meter plateau of grazing cows and 360-degree alpine panoramas, crowned by an acclaimed open-air sculpture museum.

train.note: Japan has no international trains. Matsumoto Station is served by JR East and the private Alpico Kotsu: the Azusa limited express runs from Shinjuku in Tokyo along the Chuo Main Line in about 2 hours 40 minutes, and the Shinano limited express comes up from Nagoya in roughly 2 hours. The Shinonoi Line links Matsumoto to Nagano in under an hour, and the Oito Line runs north toward Hakuba and the Northern Alps. Alpico's 14 km Kamikochi Line runs to Shin-Shimashima, where buses continue into the Kamikochi valley. Book Azusa reserved seats a month ahead in the autumn hiking season.

bus.note: There are no international buses from Japan. Alpico Kotsu (https://www.alpico.co.jp/) is the main coach operator, running highway buses from the Matsumoto Bus Terminal near the station to Shinjuku in about 3 hours 20 minutes, plus Nagoya, Osaka and Nagano, and the shuttle buses to Kamikochi and Norikura that are the only way into those valleys since private cars are banned. Nohi Bus links Matsumoto with Takayama over the Alps via Hirayu Onsen. Reserve online in advance for summer weekends, when the Kamikochi services sell out.

ferry.note: Matsumoto sits in a mountain basin in central Nagano Prefecture, far from the sea, so there are no ferry services. The only boats are sightseeing rowboats and pleasure craft on nearby alpine lakes such as Lake Aoki and Lake Kizaki.

full.name: Norikura Kogen
full.blurb: A highland plateau at the foot of 3,026-meter Mount Norikura, about two hours away by bus, with alpine ponds and waterfalls.

full.name: Shirahone Onsen
full.blurb: A remote hot spring village in the Northern Alps about two hours away, known for milky white sulfur baths.
